memo_rationale: The election must be consistent with the revised renewal provisions. The proposed design eliminates Carry and automatic concurrent positions, while retaining a separately disclosed payoff from a new purchase. Do not describe these design changes as statutory bans on every renewal.
memo_replacement: Prior transaction treatment: Section 1 shall state either “Not applicable” or “Separately authorized payoff under Section 8.2.” Any such payoff must identify the prior transaction, its agreed settlement amount, any rebate or discount, and the resulting Net Amount Funded. No prior balance is carried into the new Purchased Amount. No election or amount may remain blank when Merchant signs.
current_body: Rollover Method (renewals only): _________«25»_________. This states the method Merchant elected under Section 8.2 — Deduct or Carry — and the Purchased Amount in Section 1.3 is calculated on it. On a first-time transaction with no prior balance, this reads “Not applicable”.
my_note: Depends entirely on what we decide at 032/081/082. Sequence it after the renewal design is settled; changing the election before the mechanism is incoherent.

heading: Position and Cascade of Collections
memo_rationale: The cascade affirmatively authorizes concurrent Lombard positions, while the page’s earlier findings report an anti-stacking marketing promise. That external promise has not independently been reviewed. Either validate and revise the marketing or change the product. Proposed replacement adopts a single active position, eliminating automatic cascading and percentage confusion.
memo_replacement: Buyer shall not maintain more than one active purchase of the same Card Receipts under this Agreement or a renewal. No remittance automatically cascades to another transaction. A subsequent purchase requires a new agreement, fresh disclosures and signatures, and completion or separately authorized settlement of the prior purchase at or before the new Purchase Date under Section 8.
current_body: If Merchant has multiple active funding agreements with Buyer (each a “Position”), collections of the Specified Percentage and Estimated Daily Holdback shall be applied to the lowest-numbered Position first (Position 1 being the first-priority funding). Upon completion of any Position (i.e., upon attainment of the Completion Threshold for that Position), collections shall automatically cascade to the next active Position in ascending order. The provisions of this Section 4.15 supplement (and do not waive) the prohibition on third-party Stacking under Section 5.16; this Section governs only Buyer’s own multi-position fundings on the same Merchant.
my_note: §4.15 affirmatively authorises concurrent Lombard positions while our marketing reportedly promises no stacking. That gap is a UDAP problem before it is a contract problem. Either the marketing changes or the clause does — and the marketing has not been reviewed by anyone.

heading: Stacking Prohibited
memo_rationale: This prohibits third-party receipt sales while §6.1.13 prohibits all financing and §4.15 permits Buyer’s own stacks. Replace with a coherent rule protecting the actual sold share, and delete unrestricted sharing with any third party. The proposed narrow covenant is a commercial risk choice.
memo_replacement: Merchant shall not knowingly sell the same Purchased Receipts twice or grant an inconsistent voluntary interest prohibited by Section 4.11. Financing secured by other assets or Merchant’s retained receipts is not prohibited solely because it is financing. Before entering a proposed arrangement affecting the same purchased share, Merchant shall provide information reasonably necessary to assess the conflict. Buyer shall respond reasonably and promptly and shall use or share that information only as permitted by Section 4.7. Buyer’s own subsequent purchases are subject to Sections 4.15 and 8.
current_body: Merchant shall not, without Buyer’s prior written consent, sign any agreement for the sale of future receipts with any party other than Buyer for the duration of this Agreement. Buyer may share information regarding this Agreement with any third party in order to determine whether Merchant is in compliance with this provision.
my_note: Three clauses give three different stacking answers: §5.16 bans third-party receipt sales, §6.1.13 bans all financing, §4.15 permits our own. That incoherence is unusable in litigation and indefensible in an examination. Also delete the unrestricted third-party sharing limb.

heading: Sale of Additional Pool of Receipts; Right of First Refusal
memo_rationale: Automatic master-agreement treatment, reduction by prior Purchased Amounts, and the ROFR conflict with a new signed transaction and may misstate payoff by using original face amounts instead of current settlements. Delete this machinery in favor of §8. A ROFR is not inherently unlawful but is unnecessary to protect an already sold share.
memo_replacement: This Agreement is not a master agreement for future funding and creates no right of first refusal. Every subsequent purchase must comply with Section 8 and be separately offered, disclosed, documented, and accepted. No original or remaining amount under a prior transaction is automatically deducted from a new Purchase Price.
current_body: In the event that Merchant wishes to sell, and Buyer agrees to purchase, an additional pool (or additional pools) of Receipts, this Agreement shall serve as a Master Agreement which sets forth all of the terms and conditions governing any such sale. The parties shall execute an additional schedule for each such purchase, setting forth the Purchase Price, Specified Percentage, Estimated Daily Holdback, and Purchased Amount applicable to that additional pool of future receivables. The Purchase Price listed on such schedule shall be reduced dollar-for-dollar by Purchased Amounts then outstanding from prior purchases of Receipts by Buyer. Nothing herein shall obligate either party to sell and purchase additional pools; however, Merchant grants Buyer the right of first refusal to purchase any such pool of additional future receivables that Merchant may wish to sell.
my_note: Automatic master-agreement treatment plus reduction by prior Purchased Amounts can misstate payoff by using original face amounts rather than current settlements. Delete in favour of §8. The ROFR is lawful but unnecessary.

heading: Renewal Eligibility
memo_rationale: Renewal is not inherently unlawful, but pre-completion financing plus the cascade/Carry machinery can double-commit the same pool. Require a new offer and disclosure, a genuine net-proceeds analysis, and retirement of the old claim.
memo_replacement: Neither party is obligated to enter a subsequent purchase. Any subsequent purchase requires new underwriting based on current receipts and existing obligations, a new complete agreement, all required disclosures, and fresh acceptance. Buyer shall separately identify the additional cash Merchant receives and any old obligation settled from the new consideration. The prior purchase must be completed or expressly settled at or before the new Purchase Date, with its collection authority terminated and its ledger closed under Section 8.2. No automatic renewal, concurrent position, or continuing guaranty arises from this Agreement.
current_body: Merchant may be eligible for a renewal funding prior to full collection of the Purchased Amount under this Agreement, subject to Buyer’s underwriting approval. Any renewal shall be documented under a new Future Receivables Purchase Agreement incorporating the outstanding balance from this Agreement.
my_note: Pre-completion financing plus the cascade machinery can double-commit the same receivables pool. Require a new offer, fresh disclosures, a genuine net-proceeds figure and retirement of the old claim.

heading: Rollover Methods
memo_rationale: Carry can leave the old agreement alive while its remaining balance is included in a second Purchased Amount. Deduct may refinance unpaid financing charges, which requires honest net-proceeds and payoff treatment. The proposed design removes Carry, does not claim every refinancing of prior charges is prohibited, and requires a specific fresh election and state disclosures. [A8–A14]
memo_replacement:
No prior Remaining Balance is carried into the new Purchased Amount. Merchant may separately authorize a stated portion of a new Purchase Price to settle an identified prior transaction. Before acceptance, Buyer shall disclose the prior transaction’s current settlement amount, collections already credited, any unpaid finance charges, any applicable rebate or discount, the amount of new consideration applied to settlement, and the cash actually delivered to Merchant. Buyer shall make any additional refinancing disclosures required by law and shall not count a payoff as cash delivered to Merchant.
On the new Purchase Date, the authorized settlement shall fully extinguish the identified prior purchase, terminate its split instructions, and be recorded once in both ledgers. Buyer shall confirm that no duplicate claim or collection right remains. The new Purchased Amount equals the newly disclosed Purchase Price multiplied by its stated Factor Rate, without adding the old balance a second time. Merchant is bound only by the accepted, fully calculated offer. A changed settlement, price, or net disbursement requires corrected disclosures and renewed acceptance when required by law. No reference to “renewal” waives a required rebate or permits an unlawful charge.
current_body:
If Merchant has an outstanding Remaining Balance at the time of renewal, the balance shall be handled by whichever of the following methods Merchant elects. Under both methods the Purchase Price is the consideration for the new Purchased Amount, and Merchant may apply part of the Purchase Price to satisfy an existing obligation, whether owed to Buyer or to another funder:
(a) Deduct. The outstanding Remaining Balance is satisfied out of the Purchase Price, and appears as “Less: Prior Balance(s)” in the itemization in Section 1.4. The new Purchased Amount is Purchase Price × Factor Rate. Merchant receives a reduced disbursement because part of the Purchase Price has been applied to retire the existing obligation, in the same way as if it had been applied to retire an obligation owed to another funder. Where the obligation retired is owed to Buyer, the amount of the new financing used to pay unpaid finance charges on it is disclosed to Merchant on any state disclosure that requires it.
(b) Carry. The outstanding Remaining Balance is carried into the new Purchased Amount rather than paid off, so that the new Purchased Amount is (Purchase Price × Factor Rate) + Remaining Balance. The Remaining Balance is carried at face value and no Factor Rate is applied to it. “Less: Prior Balance(s)” in Section 1.4 is $0.00 under this method. Merchant receives the full Net Amount Funded, but the total delivery obligation increases by the rollover amount.
The Deduct or Carry method applicable to any renewal shall be elected by Merchant. Because the two methods produce different Purchased Amounts, the election is made before this Agreement is issued for signature: Buyer shall explain both methods and the Purchased Amount each produces, Merchant elects, and the elected method is recorded in Section 1 as the Rollover Method with the Purchased Amount in Section 1.3 calculated on that method. Buyer may propose a method when presenting the offer, but Merchant may require the other, in which case Buyer shall re-issue the offer priced on the method Merchant elects. Merchant is not bound by a proposed method it has not elected.
my_note: Carry can leave the old agreement alive while its balance is folded into a second Purchased Amount — that is the mechanism that produces the '$100,000 advance' that delivers $65,000. The memo's illustration should be read by whoever writes our offer language.
